title: Ethereum changes through EIPs
description: An EIP (Ethereum Improvement Proposal) is a public proposal to change Ethereum. Anyone can write one, but the network only changes once it is discussed on the core dev calls and shipped in a hard fork. We explain the EIPs that come up on the calls, simply and in depth, from the spec and the call records. Explanations are written in Korean.

flow.title: How an EIP reaches mainnet
flow.intro: Refining the proposal and deciding which fork it goes into are two separate tracks.

steps.title: Proposal
steps.body: Anyone opens a draft in the EIPs repository with the problem, the solution and a spec.

steps.title: Refinement
steps.body: Researchers and client developers review and revise it on the forum and in the repo.

steps.title: Proposed
steps.body: It is proposed for the next hard fork on a core dev call.

steps.title: Considered
steps.body: The call agrees to seriously consider it. Not final yet.

steps.title: Scheduled
steps.body: It is scheduled for the fork. Clients start implementing it.

steps.title: On mainnet
steps.body: After testnets, it activates on every node on fork day.

flow.dfi: An EIP dropped from the candidates becomes DFI (declined). It can be proposed again for a later fork.

items.def: An upgrade that activates a bundle of EIPs on one day, named like Pectra, Glamsterdam or Hegota.
The flagship feature of a fork. The fork schedule follows its readiness.
Public calls where client teams decide fork scope and timing. ACDE covers execution, ACDC consensus, ACDT testing.
A temporary test network where developers check their implementations against each other.
The side that processes transactions (EL) and the side that finalizes blocks (CL). Which one an EIP changes decides which teams own it.
EIPs that change rules every node must follow. They need a hard fork.
